preamble: Loss of glottalization combined with retraction: the velar ejective [kʼ] becomes the plain voiceless uvular stop [q]. Proto-Semitic emphatic *ḳ is usually reconstructed as an ejective *kʼ (Cantineau 1952; Kogan 2011), the value it keeps in Ethiopian Semitic (Geʽez, Amharic, Tigrinya); in Arabic, Aramaic and the Tiberian and Mizrahi Hebrew traditions it surfaces as uvular [q] (Ashkenazi, Sephardi and Israeli Hebrew have [k]). The ejective value is a reconstruction, not a direct observation. Later Arabic q > ʔ (Cairene) and q > g (Bedouin) are separate shifts.
